answer: Sybil tax: every new identity pays a non-refundable $20 entry tax before it can trade, a plume of smoke marking each new account. The tax funds an opal seal, a public registry where each paid identity is listed once and cannot be duplicated. A single sparrow pays $20 once and keeps its full share of the $3,000 pool, but a faker minting 1,000 identities pays $20,000, far more than the pool is worth, so mass forgery loses money by design.
